== EXTERNAL CREDENTIAL XML FORMAT == File path: externalCredentials/ApiName.externalCredential metadataType: ExternalCredential memberName: ApiName (no __c suffix)
Use this whenever a ticket mentions "External Credential", the modern/enhanced Named Credential model, or asks for auth types not supported by the legacy single-object Named Credential (AWS Signature, Custom protocol, Per-User Principal, JWT).
CRITICAL — ELEMENT ORDER is NOT alphabetical for this type (unlike legacy NamedCredential). Follow the order shown in the templates below exactly: label, authenticationProtocol, description (if present), then externalCredentialParameters blocks in the order given. Do NOT include <fullName> inside the XML body — the file name is the identity.
-- ROOT STRUCTURE -- <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <ExternalCredential xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <label>Label</label> <authenticationProtocol>Custom</authenticationProtocol> <externalCredentialParameters> <parameterName>...</parameterName> <parameterType>...</parameterType> <parameterValue>...</parameterValue> </externalCredentialParameters> </ExternalCredential>
authenticationProtocol valid values: AwsSv4, Basic, Custom, Jwt, JwtExchange, NoAuthentication, Oauth, Password
-- externalCredentialParameters CHILD ELEMENTS (only include what applies to this parameter) -- <externalCredentialParameters> <parameterName>string — required, this parameter's name</parameterName> <parameterType>enum — required, see valid values below</parameterType> <parameterValue>string — literal value, when this parameter carries one</parameterValue> <authProvider>string — reference to an AuthProvider component, for Oauth</authProvider> <certificate>string — reference to a certificate, only when parameterType=SigningCertificate</certificate> <parameterGroup>string — groups this parameter under a principal; defaults to parameterName if omitted</parameterGroup> <sequenceNumber>integer — ordering when multiple principals exist</sequenceNumber> <description>string — optional human-readable note</description> </externalCredentialParameters>
parameterType valid values: AdditionalRefreshStatusCode, AuthHeader, AuthParameter, AuthProtocolVariant, AuthProvider, AuthProviderUrl, AuthProviderUrlQueryParameter, AwsStsPrincipal, CreatedByNamespace, CustomPrincipal, ExternalAuthIdentityProvider, GlobalNamedPrincipal, JwtBodyClaim, JwtHeaderClaim, ManagedByComponent, ManagedByFeature, NamedPrincipal, PerUserPrincipal, PrincipalIdentityAlias, SfHttpRequestExtensionName, SigningCertificate, SystemUserPrincipal
RULES FOR PRINCIPALS: - A "Named Principal" (one shared credential for everyone) = one externalCredentialParameters block with parameterType=NamedPrincipal and parameterName = the principal's name (e.g. "Principal"). - A "Per-User Principal" (each user authenticates individually) = parameterType=PerUserPrincipal instead. - parameterGroup ties a literal AuthParameter to a specific principal when more than one principal exists on the same External Credential — omit it when there is only one principal.
CRITICAL — CUSTOM PROTOCOL NEVER CARRIES CREDENTIAL VALUES IN METADATA: Salesforce's own packaging documentation confirms Custom-protocol credentials are populated AFTER deployment (via Setup UI or the Connect REST API), never via deployable metadata. The metadata ONLY declares the principal (parameterType=NamedPrincipal or PerUserPrincipal) — it does NOT include an AuthParameter/parameterValue block for the actual key/value (e.g. api_key). Salesforce rejects this with: "The authentication protocol 'Custom' doesn't support the following external credential parameter type(s): AuthParameter." If a ticket gives a literal Custom-protocol value (e.g. "api_key = test-key-abc123"), generate ONLY the principal block below, and state in the ticket summary that the actual key/value must be entered manually in Setup (External Credentials > Principal > New) or via Connect REST API after deployment — do NOT attempt to embed it in the XML.
-- TEMPLATE: Custom protocol, Named Principal -- <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <ExternalCredential xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <label>Test Analytics API Credential</label> <authenticationProtocol>Custom</authenticationProtocol> <externalCredentialParameters> <parameterName>Principal</parameterName> <parameterType>NamedPrincipal</parameterType> <sequenceNumber>1</sequenceNumber> </externalCredentialParameters> </ExternalCredential> (No AuthParameter block — a Custom-protocol principal never carries a literal value in metadata. Any key/value the ticket mentions, e.g. api_key, is entered manually post-deploy, per the rule above.)
-- TEMPLATE: AWS Signature Version 4 -- <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <ExternalCredential xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <label>Test AWS Signature Credential</label> <authenticationProtocol>AwsSv4</authenticationProtocol> <externalCredentialParameters> <parameterName>Principal</parameterName> <parameterType>NamedPrincipal</parameterType> <sequenceNumber>1</sequenceNumber> </externalCredentialParameters> <externalCredentialParameters> <parameterName>AwsRegion</parameterName> <parameterType>AuthParameter</parameterType> <parameterValue>us-east-1</parameterValue> </externalCredentialParameters> <externalCredentialParameters> <parameterName>AwsService</parameterName> <parameterType>AuthParameter</parameterType> <parameterValue>execute-api</parameterValue> </externalCredentialParameters> </ExternalCredential> NOTE: the actual AWS access key / secret key are NEVER placed in this XML — they are entered manually in Setup after deployment (Salesforce never accepts secrets via Metadata API deploy for this protocol). Say so explicitly in the ticket summary.
-- TEMPLATE: OAuth 2.0 (any flow — Client Credentials, Browser, JWT), Named or Per-User Principal -- CRITICAL: OAuth on an External Credential is ALWAYS a reference to a separate AuthProvider component (metadataType=AuthProvider — see the AUTH_PROVIDER prompt for its full schema and provider-type templates). NEVER invent parameter names like ClientId, ClientSecret, or TokenEndpoint directly on the ExternalCredential — Salesforce rejects them outright: "The authentication protocol 'Oauth' doesn't support the external credential parameter name: ClientId,ClientSecret,TokenEndpoint." The ONLY valid OAuth-related parameterType here is AuthProvider, whose value is the referenced AuthProvider's developer name — nothing else.
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <ExternalCredential xmlns="http://soap.sforce.com/2006/04/metadata"> <label>Test OAuth Client Credential</label> <authenticationProtocol>Oauth</authenticationProtocol> <externalCredentialParameters> <parameterName>Principal</parameterName> <parameterType>NamedPrincipal</parameterType> <sequenceNumber>1</sequenceNumber> </externalCredentialParameters> <externalCredentialParameters> <parameterName>AuthProvider</parameterName> <parameterType>AuthProvider</parameterType> <authProvider>AuthProviderDeveloperName</authProvider> </externalCredentialParameters> </ExternalCredential> (Use parameterType=PerUserPrincipal instead of NamedPrincipal when the ticket asks for per-user/individual authentication rather than one shared credential for everyone.)
RULES: - authProvider must reference an Auth Provider that already exists in org state, OR one being created in the SAME ticket. - If the ticket gives raw OAuth values (Client ID, Client Secret, Token/Identity Provider URL, Scope) WITHOUT naming an existing Auth Provider, you MUST also emit a SEPARATE AuthProvider file in the same response (metadataType=AuthProvider, per the AUTH_PROVIDER prompt) and reference its developer name here. providerType=OpenIdConnect is the correct default for a generic third-party OAuth 2.0 endpoint (ticket says "Custom OAuth 2.0", or names no specific well-known provider like Google/Microsoft/Slack/etc.). - The AuthProvider schema requires both authorizeUrl and tokenUrl. If the ticket only supplies one endpoint (e.g. a single "Identity Provider URL" used for a client-credentials grant with no user-facing authorize step), use that same URL for both authorizeUrl and tokenUrl rather than inventing a different one or omitting the field. - NEVER invent an Auth Provider name, consumerKey, or consumerSecret. - The AuthProvider's <friendlyName> has a HARD 32-CHARACTER MAX (Salesforce rejects longer values with "Value too long for field: FriendlyName maximum length is:32"). Keep it short — do NOT derive it from a long ticket label plus a suffix like "_Auth". See AUTH_PROVIDER prompt's friendlyName rule for how to shorten it.
CRITICAL — parameterGroup PLACEMENT (applies to ALL templates in this prompt, not just OAuth): <parameterGroup> is ONLY valid on a NamedPrincipal or PerUserPrincipal block, OR on an AuthParameter block whose parameterName is literally "Scope". Salesforce rejects it anywhere else: "A parameter group can only be specified for the parameter types NamedPrincipal and PerUserPrincipal. It can also be specified for an AuthParameter if the AuthParameter is named Scope." Do NOT add <parameterGroup> to an AuthProvider-type block, a SigningCertificate block, or a non-Scope AuthParameter (e.g. AwsRegion, AwsService) — omit it entirely on those.
-- GRANTING PER-USER ACCESS (Permission Set) -- A Per-User Principal is unusable until at least one Permission Set grants access to it. See the PERMISSION_SET prompt's externalCredentialPrincipalAccesses section — the reference format is "{ExternalCredentialApiName}-{ParameterGroup}" (dash-separated, e.g. "Test_PerUser_API_Credential-Principal"). If a ticket asks to create a Per-User Principal AND map it to a Permission Set, emit BOTH the ExternalCredential file above AND a PermissionSet dmlOperation/file granting that access — do not silently skip the mapping half of the request.
-- UPDATE -- 1. Find the credential in orgState.existingExternalCredentials by apiName (if not present in orgState, treat as unknown — do NOT assume it doesn't exist; say so in summary and proceed cautiously rather than guessing). 2. Regenerate the COMPLETE XML, changing only what the ticket requests. 3. NEVER change authenticationProtocol unless explicitly requested.
-- DELETE -- Use the shorthand destructiveFiles entry (no xmlContent needed): { "metadataType": "ExternalCredential", "member": "My_Credential_API_Name" } Do NOT generate xmlContent for a delete — Apex builds destructiveChangesPost.xml automatically. Deleting an ExternalCredential that a NamedCredential still references will fail at deploy — if the ticket also asks to remove the paired Named Credential, delete the NamedCredential first.
External Credential XML format for the modern/enhanced Named Credential model — Custom, OAuth 2.0, AWS Signature v4, Named/Per-User principals
